_comment: Storage. The OCC governance container holds workflows, decisions, rules, the audit chain and the versioned configuration packages (_global/config-packages/{layer}/…). Same storage account as the MI API's processed-v2; a DIFFERENT container.
name: TRAKT_BLOB_CONNECTION

_comment: Writable scratch. App Service gives every app a writable /tmp; the defaults in operations_control are RELATIVE paths (.ops_state/…) which would land inside the read-only-ish deployment root, so set both explicitly.
name: TRAKT_OPS_STAGING_ROOT

_comment: Operator/administrator identity. FAIL-CLOSED: operations_control/api/auth.py returns HTTP 503 on EVERY route while this is unset or unparseable, so the service is unusable until it is set. JSON map of token -> {name, clients, role}. clients:["*"] = all clients; role:"admin" grants the /ops/admin/config/* area (require_admin). Omit role for an ordinary operator. Use long random tokens and store this as a Key Vault reference, not a literal.
name: TRAKT_OPS_OPERATORS

_comment: Browser origins allowed to call this API. Comma-separated, EXACT origins. There is deliberately no wildcard: operations_control/api/app.py feeds this straight into CORSMiddleware allow_origins, and '*' would let any site drive administrator configuration actions with a stolen token. Must list the deployed React OCC origin.
name: TRAKT_OPS_CORS_ORIGINS

_comment: Serving. One worker: the OCC engine runs workflows on background threads and reconciles interrupted runs on startup, so each extra worker is another engine competing for the same blob leases. Timeout 300s covers a long governed stage (onboarding / Annex 2 XML build) without the worker being killed mid-run.
name: OPS_API_WORKERS

_comment: Shared platform containers. The OCC resolves client/portfolio records through the source registry and publishes approved packs through the existing promotion path (apps.blob_trigger_app.layout.Layout.from_env + ProductionPersistence), so these must match the values the blob trigger and the MI API already use. Defaults shown; set them explicitly so both services cannot drift apart.
name: TRAKT_SOURCE_REGISTRY_URI

_comment: Outbound onboarding email (trakt_mail). OFF unless this switch is an explicit opt-in token, and OFF if ANY of the four settings below is absent — the OCC then keeps its RecordOnlyAdapter, which states plainly that nothing was sent. Turning it on changes only the receipt: the pack workflow DRAFTED -> HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED -> APPROVED_TO_SEND -> SENT and its human approval gate are unchanged, and nothing can be sent that a person has not approved.
name: TRAKT_MAIL_OUTBOUND_ENABLED

_comment: The Entra app registration 'Trakt OCC Mail'. Graph APPLICATION permissions Mail.Send (to send) and Mail.Read (to read the message back out of Sent Items for its message id), admin-consented, and scoped to this ONE mailbox with an Exchange Application Access Policy. Verify with Test-ApplicationAccessPolicy before use.
name: TRAKT_MAIL_TENANT_ID

_comment: Store as a Key Vault REFERENCE, never a literal, and never in source control: @Microsoft.KeyVault(SecretUri=https://<vault>.vault.azure.net/secrets/trakt-mail-client-secret/). Rotate on the app registration and update the secret; no redeploy is needed.
name: TRAKT_MAIL_CLIENT_SECRET

_comment: The mailbox every OCC communication is sent FROM and read BACK IN. Must be the mailbox the Application Access Policy scopes the app to. Use a DEDICATED mailbox: the policy scopes the application to a whole mailbox and cannot scope it to a folder, so pointing this at a mailbox that also receives unrelated business email gives the application read access to all of it.
name: TRAKT_MAIL_MAILBOX

_comment: Inbound client replies (trakt_mail.inbound / trakt_mail.ingest). A SEPARATE switch from the outbound one, because sending a pack and reading a mailbox are different capabilities: a deployment may hold either without the other. OFF unless this is an explicit opt-in token. With it on, an operator can see what has arrived and take a reply into a case; nothing polls and nothing is ingested unattended. A client's FILES are registered through the same governed method an operator's upload uses; a client's WORDS are recorded for the operator to read and are never applied to a case on their own.
name: TRAKT_MAIL_INBOUND_ENABLED

_comment: OPTIONAL. The folder replies are read from; defaults to the inbox. Naming a dedicated folder (fed by an Outlook rule) is how a deployment that MUST share a mailbox narrows what the reader looks at. Understand what that is and is not: the Application Access Policy still grants the application the whole mailbox, so this is a process control, not a technical one.
name: TRAKT_MAIL_INBOUND_FOLDER

_comment: OPTIONAL, and advised for the first controlled onboarding. Comma-separated addresses or @domain suffixes whose mail may be ingested; EMPTY MEANS NO RESTRICTION. A message is dropped before its attachments are downloaded, so this genuinely limits what the deployment reads rather than what it acts on.
name: TRAKT_MAIL_SENDER_ALLOWLIST

_comment: OPTIONAL inbound mechanics; the defaults are the supported configuration. INBOUND_MAX bounds how many messages one read examines, because the read happens inside an API request. MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES bounds a single download; an attachment over it is REPORTED to the operator with its size, never silently skipped.

OPTIONAL, and strongly advised for the first controlled onboarding. Comma-separated addresses or @domain suffixes this deployment may send to; EMPTY MEANS NO RESTRICTION. Set it to your own address while the capability is being proven, so a stale or mistyped contact on a case cannot reach a real client. Remove it once the first real client is onboarded.
name: TRAKT_MAIL_RECIPIENT_ALLOWLIST

_comment: OPTIONAL delivery mechanics; the defaults are the supported configuration. sendMail answers 202 with no body, so Sent Items is re-read to recover the real message id; these bound that read-back. Confirmation is best-effort and never fails a send that Graph accepted.
The OCC Agent tab itself. The mail adapter is only ever reached through it, so with this unset no route exists and nothing can be sent.
name: OCC_AGENT_SYNTHETIC_ENABLED

_comment: Governed runtime mode. Leave UNSET in production: trakt_core defaults to 'production', which is what refuses fixture/synthetic source data. Listed here only so nobody adds it by accident.
